reason: E1 states that higher particle speeds in HVOF result in lower in-flight oxidation and better coating densities, supporting the velocity–oxidation–density link, but it does not address fuel-to-oxygen ratio tuning, FeCoNiCrAl, or the specific HVAF-i7 system. E3 and E4 describe general HVOF/HVAF processes and parameters for other HEA compositions but provide no direct evidence that adjusting the fuel-to-oxygen ratio increases velocity or thickness for the target alloy and torch. The cited evidence is only loosely related to the key premises, leaving most unsupported.
premises: Higher in-flight particle velocity improves splat deformation and consolidation
Increasing fuel-to-oxygen ratio in HVAF increases particle velocity
Higher velocity reduces in-flight oxidation due to shorter dwell time
Improved splat formation leads to thicker, more adherent coatings
The effect holds for FeCoNiCrAl HEA with 15–45 μm powder in HVAF-i7
